There is a thing called starter dough/starter bread. It is leavened dough that is added to unleavened dough - flour, water, sugars, etc - to make it rise.

Starter dough and unleavened dough look exactly the same from the outside, but once starter dough gets added to flour, water, etc, it causes a runaway leavening action - it can't be removed.

There was a show a while ago on BBC about how the victorians/before made bread and pastries, and part of that was to have a stock of leavening dough on hand, and it typically carried over from batch to batch - ie, the leavening dough was added to the batch, all stirred up and left to rise, then some of that dough was taken as the starter dough for the next big batch.

(And big batch was like 100lbs of dough for a bakery, not the standard "one loaf" type baking)
